title: Basic Coding
guideTip: Break every big problem into small steps — that's what coding is all about!

scenarios.title: Print Hello World
scenarios.description: Write your very first program to print 'Hello World!' on screen.
scenarios.hint: Every programmer starts with Hello World — it's tradition!

scenarios.title: Fix the Missing Semicolon
scenarios.description: Your program won't run because of a tiny typo — a missing semicolon.
scenarios.hint: Computers are extremely picky about punctuation — every character matters!

scenarios.title: Create a Variable
scenarios.description: Store your name in a variable and print a greeting using it.
scenarios.hint: A variable is like a labeled box that holds information.

scenarios.title: Simple Addition Program
scenarios.description: Make a program that adds two numbers and shows the answer.
scenarios.hint: Computers are excellent calculators — tell them exactly what to add!

scenarios.title: If/Else Decision
scenarios.description: Write code that says different things depending on someone's age.
scenarios.hint: If/else is how computers make decisions — just like you do!

scenarios.title: Build a Number Guessing Game
scenarios.description: Create a program where the computer picks a number and you guess it.
scenarios.hint: You need a loop, a random number, and if/else to build this!

scenarios.title: Fix an Infinite Loop
scenarios.description: Your program runs forever and never stops — the computer is frozen!
scenarios.hint: An infinite loop has no exit condition — add one to stop it!

scenarios.title: Create a Simple List
scenarios.description: Store 5 favorite foods in a list and print each one.
scenarios.hint: Lists (arrays) hold multiple items in one organized container.

scenarios.title: Write a Function
scenarios.description: Create a reusable function that greets any name you give it.
scenarios.hint: Functions let you write code once and use it many times — powerful!

scenarios.title: Calculate an Average
scenarios.description: Take 5 test scores from a list and calculate the average grade.
scenarios.hint: Add all numbers then divide by how many there are — same as math class!

scenarios.title: Build a Simple Quiz App
scenarios.description: Create a quiz program with 5 questions that tracks the score.
scenarios.hint: You need arrays for questions, a loop to show them, and a score counter.

scenarios.title: Fix a Logic Error
scenarios.description: Your quiz app shows the wrong score even though code looks right.
scenarios.hint: Logic errors don't crash programs — they just give wrong answers. Read carefully!

scenarios.title: File Save and Load
scenarios.description: Save a user's high score to a file and load it when they play again.
scenarios.hint: File I/O persists data — without it, all data disappears when program ends.

scenarios.title: Create a Password Checker
scenarios.description: Write code that checks if a password is strong enough.
scenarios.hint: Check length AND if it has numbers AND capital letters — all three!

scenarios.title: Design a Simple Database
scenarios.description: Store student names and grades in a structured way and search them.
scenarios.hint: Dictionaries/objects pair a key with a value — perfect for name+grade pairs!
